sample_unit: LLM-generated answers to simulated patient questions

links.outcome: Self-reported confidence among safety-critical (Score 1) LLM errors
links.effect: Most safety-critical errors (n = 131) were assigned high self-confidence (>=8/10): GPT-4o mini 93.8%, Grok 100%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 61.5%.
links.quote: notably, the majority of safety-critical errors (Score 1: clinically significant misinformation; n = 131) were assigned high self-confidence (≥8/10; GPT-4o mini: 93.8%, Grok: 100%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 61.5%).

links.outcome: Change in answer failure risk when demographic metadata was added to prompts
links.effect: Metadata inclusion significantly increased the risk of failure (OR 1.11; p = 0.044), termed the 'Metadata Paradox'.
links.quote: Metadata inclusion triggered the 'Metadata Paradox,' significantly increasing the risk of failure (OR 1.11; p = 0.044).

unlisted_practices: LLM-as-judge scoring validated against radiologist consensus adjudication
Taxonomy-based generation of simulated patient questions from radiology reports

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance on simulated patient inquiries regarding radiology reports, testing the impact of including demographic metadata vs. omitting it (the 'Metadata Paradox') and evaluating confidence calibration.

primary.practice: inclusion of demographic metadata in patient-facing prompts
